Эта техника может особенно заинтересовать вас, если вы склонны откладывать дела, считая их слишком сложными или не приносящими удовольствия.

На первом этапе в одну колонку запишите одну или две задачи, выполнение которых вы откладываете.

Если задача требует значительных временных и усилий, лучше всего разбить её на несколько маленьких этапов, каждый из которых занимает не более 15-20 минут.

Далее, во второй колонке оцените на шкале от 0 до 100%, насколько сложной, по вашему мнению, окажется выполнение этой задачи.

<important>Если задача кажется вам лёгкой, поставьте низкую оценку — например, 10 или 20%. Если задача кажется более сложной, уместно будет написать 80 или 90%.</important>

В третьей колонке, также используя процентную шкалу, запишите ваш прогноз относительно того, сколько удовольствия принесёт выполнение задачи.

Приступайте к выполнению задачи только после того, как запишете свои прогнозы.

<q author="Джек Лондон">Вы не можете ждать вдохновения. Вы должны идти ему навстречу с работой.</q>
en.oldText:
This technique is especially helpful if you tend to put things off because they feel too hard or not enjoyable.

First, in one column, write down one or two tasks you’ve been postponing.

If a task requires significant time and effort, break it into several small stages, each taking no more than 15–20 minutes.

Next, in the second column, rate—on a scale from 0 to 100%—how difficult you expect the task to be.

If the task feels easy, give it a low rating—say, 10 or 20%. If it feels harder, 80 or 90% may be appropriate.

In the third column, also using percentages, write your forecast of how much enjoyment the task will bring.

Begin only after you’ve recorded your predictions.
en.newText:
This technique may be particularly helpful if you tend to put things off because they feel too difficult or unrewarding.

In the first stage, write one or two tasks you’ve been procrastinating on in one column.

If a task requires significant time and effort, it’s best to break it down into several small steps, each taking no more than 15–20 minutes.

Next, in the second column, use a scale from 0 to 100% to rate how difficult you think completing the task will be.

<important>If a task seems easy, give it a low rating—for example, 10% or 20%. If it seems more difficult, a rating of 80% or 90% would be appropriate.</important>

In the third column, also using a percentage scale, record your prediction of how much enjoyment completing the task will bring.

Only start working on the task after you have written down your predictions.

Последнее когнитивное искажение, которое мы подробно рассмотрим, называется "Чтение мыслей". Это одна из ошибок мышления, когда мы убеждены, что знаем, что думает о нас другой человек, и часто предполагаем, что он думает что-то плохое. Это может привести к тревожности, различным страхам, а иногда и к паранойе. Это может быть причиной конфликтов, обид, ссор и, конечно, депрессии. Мы не можем изменить ситуации, которые жизнь нам преподносит, но мы можем изменить нашу способность переживать их.
en.oldText:
The last cognitive distortion we’ll look at in detail is called “mind reading.”

This thinking error shows up when we’re convinced we know what someone else thinks of us—and we often assume it’s something negative.

When we rely on mind reading, we’re often wrong about what others think, which can seriously sour our mood.

We’re mistaken because we don’t actually know what another person is thinking or why they acted the way they did.

This can fuel anxiety, various fears, and sometimes even paranoia. It can spark conflicts, hurt feelings, arguments—and, of course, depression.
en.newText:

This is a thinking error where we’re convinced we know what another person is thinking about us, often assuming they’re thinking something negative. If we rely too heavily on mind reading, we may misinterpret how others see us, which can seriously impact our mood.

We often make mistakes without even realizing what another person is actually thinking or why they acted the way they did.

This can lead to anxiety, various fears, and sometimes even paranoia. It can also cause conflict, resentment, arguments, and, of course, depression. We cannot change the situations life presents to us, but we can change our ability to experience them.

Мы можем считывать мимику и жесты других людей, но это не значит, что человек, косо посмотревший на нас, обязательно подумал о нас плохо. Мы принимаем свои мысли за истину и начинаем действовать, исходя из них, а не из вероятности других вариантов. Вот несколько способов работы с "чтением мыслей":

    Осознание

Чтобы убедиться в этом вы так же можете провести ряд экспериментов. Записывайте то, что, как вы считаете, думают о вас люди, а после проверяйте. Способом проверки может быть как прямой разговор с человеком, так и наблюдение за его поступками в отношении вас. Мы не видим вещи такими, какие они есть. Мы видим их такими, какие мы сами.
en.oldText:
Examples:

I won’t tell her how I feel because she’ll think I’m weak.

He definitely won’t like my work, because I’m not happy with it myself.

She’s looking at me strangely—she must think I’m fat.

Of course, in all these cases there’s some chance people will think that way, be dissatisfied, or see you as weak.

But that chance is much lower than it seems. We can read facial expressions and body language, but a sideways glance doesn’t prove someone thought badly of us.

We take our thoughts as truth and start acting on them instead of considering other possibilities.

Here are a few ways to work with “mind reading”:

Awareness

Start noticing these thoughts and ask yourself, “Can I really read other people’s minds?”

Obviously, you can’t. To prove it to yourself, try running a few experiments: write down what you think people believe about you, and then check.

You can check either by having a direct conversation or by observing the person’s actions toward you.

en.ru:
Перфекционизм может неожиданно выступать как симптом, так и причина депрессии.

Для многих высокие стандарты и требования к себе и окружающим кажутся движущей силой. Однако, когда ожидания становятся нереалистичными, они могут превратиться в ловушку, ведущую к постоянному ощущению недостаточности, непрекращающейся критике и, как итог, к депрессии.

«Перфекционизм» означает стремление к идеалу. Существуют различные его формы:

Личностно-ориентированный, или аутоперфекционизм, характеризуется внутренним стремлением к совершенству. Люди этого типа могут бессонно проводить ночи, перепроверяя отчёты на наличие ошибок, не покидать дом из-за недостаточно аккуратной причёски, испытывать глубокое чувство вины за малейшие промахи и постоянно чувствовать себя недостаточно хорошими.

Внешне-ориентированный перфекционизм требует совершенства от других, как в случае с родителями, ожидающими отличных оценок от своих детей, или руководителем, требующим от сотрудников безукоризненной работы.

Чтобы понять, страдаете ли вы деструктивным перфекционизмом, обратите внимание на такие признаки, как непреклонная потребность в совершенстве, зависимость от мнений других, страх разочаровать, стремление к недостижимым целям, неспособность принять критику и чрезмерную строгость к себе и другим.

<q author="Лев Толстой">Если вы ищете совершенства, вы никогда не будете удовлетворены.</q>
en.oldText:
Perfectionism can unexpectedly act as both a symptom and a cause of depression.

For many, high standards and demands on oneself and others can feel like a driving force. However, when expectations become unrealistic, they can turn into a trap—leading to a constant sense of not measuring up, relentless criticism, and, ultimately, depression.

“Perfectionism” means striving for the ideal. It takes different forms:

Self-oriented perfectionism is marked by an inner push toward flawlessness. People of this type may spend sleepless nights rechecking reports for errors, avoid leaving home because their hair isn’t neat enough, feel deep guilt over minor slips, and chronically feel “not good enough.”

Other-oriented perfectionism demands perfection from others—like parents expecting top grades from their children or a manager insisting on impeccable performance from employees.

To understand whether you’re dealing with maladaptive perfectionism, watch for signs such as an uncompromising need for perfection, dependence on others’ opinions, fear of disappointing people, pursuit of unattainable goals, intolerance of criticism, and excessive strictness toward yourself and others.
en.newText:
Perfectionism can unexpectedly act as both a symptom and a cause of depression.

For many, high standards and strict demands on themselves and others feel like a driving force. However, when expectations become unrealistic, they can turn into a trap, leading to a constant sense of inadequacy, relentless self-criticism, and, eventually, depression.

“Perfectionism” means striving for the ideal. It takes various forms:

Self-oriented perfectionism is characterized by an internal drive for perfection. People with this trait might spend sleepless nights rechecking reports for errors, refuse to leave the house because their hair isn’t neat enough, feel deep guilt over the smallest slips, and constantly feel like they aren’t good enough.

Other-oriented perfectionism involves demanding perfection from others—such as parents expecting straight A’s from their children, or a manager requiring flawless work from their employees.

To understand if you’re struggling with unhelpful perfectionism, look for signs such as an unrelenting need for perfection, dependency on others’ opinions, fear of disappointing people, striving for unreachable goals, an inability to accept criticism, and being overly harsh with yourself and others.

en.oldText:
If you recognize yourself in these descriptions, don’t lose heart. There are effective ways to move beyond perfectionism.

It’s important to see the paradox at the core of perfectionism: perfection is an illusion.

Everything in the world can be improved, and the quest for an absolute ideal is destined to disappoint.

Once you grasp this, you can begin freeing yourself from perfectionism’s grip—shifting your efforts toward realistic goals and learning to find joy in the world’s and your own imperfections.

To change anything, it helps to be clear about why you need that change.

If you view perfectionism as purely helpful and see nothing problematic about it, meaningful change is unlikely.

Let’s start by weighing the pros and cons of perfectionism.

It certainly has upsides—high standards can encourage diligent work. But when faced with mistakes, you may turn that same standard into harsh self-criticism.

There’s a difference between adaptive and maladaptive perfectionism.

Adaptive perfectionism can strengthen persistence and responsibility, helping you reach goals without needless self-criticism or fear of mistakes.

Maladaptive perfectionism, in turn, breeds excessive demands on yourself and others and anxiety about any misstep, which can lead to anxiety, depression, and procrastination.

The boundary between the two can be very thin.
en.newText:
If you recognize yourself in these descriptions, don’t lose hope. There are effective ways to work through perfectionism.

However, it is important to realize that at the very heart of perfectionism lies a paradox: perfection is an illusion.

In this world, everything can be improved, and the pursuit of absolute perfection is destined to end in disappointment.

<important>Realizing this can be the first step toward breaking free from the shackles of perfectionism, allowing you to focus on achieving realistic goals and learning to find joy in the imperfection of the world and yourself.</important>

To work through something, you must first clearly recognize the need to do so.

If you believe perfectionism is helpful and see nothing wrong with it, it will be difficult to make any changes.

Let’s start by looking at the pros and cons of perfectionism.

<instagram ids="18045768971222812">

It certainly has positive aspects; for example, high standards can encourage hard work. However, when faced with mistakes, you might become overly self-critical.

There is a difference between adaptive and unhelpful perfectionism.

Adaptive perfectionism can strengthen your persistence and responsibility, helping you reach your goals without unnecessary self-criticism or fear of making mistakes.

At the same time, unhelpful perfectionism leads to excessive demands on yourself and others, and constant worry over every mistake, which can trigger anxiety, depression, and procrastination.

The line between these two types is very thin.

Оспаривание мыслей

Задайте себе вопросы: «Какие у меня есть доказательства, подтверждающие эти мысли? А какие есть аргументы против?». Эта техника позволит формализировать и взвесить ваши предположения. Обычно мы рассуждаем не слишком рационально, но когда мы проводим сравнение "за" и "против", мы вынуждены более задействовать критическое мышление.

Поиск альтернатив

Спросите себя: «О чём ещё мог подумать этот человек?» Для тех, кто готов пойти дальше, открытый и честный разговор может помочь разрешить многие недопонимания. Вместо того чтобы мучиться своими предположениями, лучше спросить у человека напрямую. Не стоит думать, что мыслительные ошибки являются признаком серьёзной психической патологии. Они присутствуют у каждого из нас в той или иной степени. Важно то, насколько часто они возникают и что мы с ними делаем: либо верим этим искажённым мыслям на все 100% и испытываем отрицательные эмоции, либо подвергаем их сомнению и анализу, приходя к более точному и многогранному видению ситуации. Работа над когнитивными искажениями может потребовать времени и усилий, но она способна значительно улучшить ваше эмоциональное благополучие и отношения с окружающими.
en.oldText:
Challenging thoughts

Ask yourself: “What evidence supports these thoughts? And what evidence contradicts them?”

This technique helps you formalize and weigh your assumptions.

We’re not always very rational, but when we compare the “for” and “against,” we’re forced to engage critical thinking more fully.

Considering alternatives

Ask yourself: “What else might this person have been thinking?”

If you’re ready to go further, open and honest conversation can resolve many misunderstandings.

Instead of torturing yourself with assumptions, it’s better to ask the person directly.

Don’t assume thinking errors are signs of a serious mental disorder.

Everyone has them to some degree.

What matters is how often they occur and what we do with them: either we believe these distorted thoughts 100% and suffer the emotional consequences, or we question and analyze them and arrive at a more accurate, nuanced view of the situation.

Working on cognitive distortions can take time and effort, but it can significantly improve your emotional well-being and your relationships.
en.newText:
Challenging your thoughts

Ask yourself: “What evidence do I have that supports these thoughts? And what evidence do I have against them?” This technique will help you formalize and weigh your assumptions. We don’t usually reason very rationally, but when we weigh the “pros” and “cons,” we’re forced to engage our critical thinking more deeply.

Finding alternatives

Ask yourself: “What else could this person be thinking?” For those ready to go further, an open and honest conversation can help resolve many misunderstandings. Instead of struggling with your assumptions, it’s better to ask the person directly. Don’t assume that cognitive distortions are a sign of serious mental pathology. They are present in all of us to some degree. What matters is how often they occur and what we do about them: we can either believe these distorted thoughts 100% and experience negative emotions, or we can question and analyze them, leading to a more accurate and nuanced view of the situation. Working on cognitive distortions may take time and effort, but it can significantly improve your mental well-being and your relationships with those around you.
